summary: A hand-written OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect authorization server in TypeScript on node:http and node:crypto, with zero runtime dependencies. Stage 1 (done, 125 tests at the time): Authorization Code flow with mandatory PKCE (S256 only; plain and missing PKCE refused), state passed through, exact redirect_uri matching, single-use 60-second codes whose reuse revokes the tokens already issued from them; clients from a static config file (public clients, and confidential clients with client_secret_basic and scrypt-hashed secrets); a minimal login form with scrypt-hashed passwords, a CSRF synchronizer token bound to a login-transaction cookie and constant-time comparisons; ES256 JWT access tokens (typ at+jwt, iss aud sub exp iat jti scope client_id, 300 s); opaque refresh tokens stored as SHA-256 hashes, rotated on every use, with reuse detection that revokes the whole token family; OIDC id_token with nonce and at_hash, discovery, JWKS with RFC 7638 kid, userinfo; RFC 7009 revocation for refresh tokens; OAuth-format errors and no-store on token responses. Storage is in memory behind small interfaces. Interop tests: jose verifies our tokens through our JWKS endpoint, and openid-client runs the whole code + PKCE flow, userinfo, refresh and revocation. 15 mutation checks (rule broken on purpose, matching test turned red) found one weak test, which was fixed. Stage 2 (done 2026-11-21, 177 tests): a file-backed store with node:fs only (append-only JSON-lines log, write-ahead with fsync, replay through the same apply function, compaction at start via temp file + rename; torn last line dropped, corrupt middle line refuses to start; only hashes on disk) proven by tests that restart the server on the same data directory; signing-key rotation with overlap (next key pre-published in JWKS, one active key, retired key published for the longest token lifetime, automatic rotation by age, private keys generated into the data dir with mode 0600); a login session cookie and OIDC RP-initiated logout (end_session_endpoint, required and verified id_token_hint, exact post_logout_redirect_uri match, state passthrough, the session's token families revoked); id_token on refresh. New interop: jose across a key rotation, openid-client buildEndSessionUrl and the refreshed id_token. 25 more mutation checks; one gap found and fixed (the write-ahead test could not see the write/apply order), one (keys.json file mode) invisible on Windows, where its test is skipped, and caught when the suite was run on Linux. NOT done: database store and more than one process per data dir, runtime expiry sweep, keys encrypted at rest / KMS, SSO with the session (prompt=none), logout without a hint, front/back-channel logout, consent, client credentials, DPoP/mTLS, login rate limiting, any measurement or deployment.

pitch.intro_30s: Maine ek OAuth 2.0 aur OpenID Connect authorization server khud likha hai, TypeScript mein, sirf node:http aur node:crypto par, koi runtime library nahi. Authorization Code flow PKCE ke saath hai (sirf S256), redirect_uri exact match hota hai, code ek hi baar chalta hai aur reuse par uske tokens revoke hote hain. Access token ES256 JWT hai, refresh tokens har use par rotate hote hain aur purana token wapas aaye toh poori family revoke. 125 tests hain, aur jose aur openid-client jaisi independent libraries ke saath interop test bhi pass hote hain.
pitch.explain_2min:
Yeh H14 hai: ek authorization server, jaise Auth0 ya Keycloak ka chhota hissa, lekin haath se likha taaki main har security rule samajh sakun.

Flow aise chalta hai. Client (jaise ek SPA) user ko /authorize par bhejta hai client_id, redirect_uri, scope, state, nonce aur PKCE code_challenge ke saath. Server pehle client aur redirect_uri check karta hai -- exact string match, koi prefix nahi. Agar yeh galat hai toh server redirect nahi karta, seedha error page dikhata hai, warna woh open redirector ban jayega. Baaki errors (plain PKCE, galat scope) redirect ke saath state lekar jaate hain.

Phir login form aata hai. Form mein ek CSRF token hai jo ek HttpOnly cookie wale login transaction se bandha hai. Password scrypt se hashed hai, aur unknown user ke liye bhi dummy scrypt chalta hai taaki timing se pata na chale ki user exist karta hai.

Login sahi hone par server ek random code banata hai, uska sirf SHA-256 hash store karta hai, aur redirect_uri par code aur state bhejta hai. Code 60 second chalta hai aur ek hi baar. Token endpoint par client code ke saath code_verifier bhejta hai; server SHA-256(verifier) ko stored challenge se constant-time compare karta hai.

Response mein ES256 JWT access token (5 minute), opaque refresh token aur openid scope par id_token aata hai. Refresh token har use par naya milta hai. Agar purana token dobara aaye -- matlab kisi ne chura liya -- toh poori token family revoke hoti hai.

Verification: 125 tests, jinme real HTTP server ephemeral port par chalta hai. jose hamare JWKS se tokens verify karta hai aur openid-client poora flow chalata hai. Maine 15 rules jaan-boojh ke tode aur har baar matching test red hua; ek kamzor test mila jo fix kiya. Honest limitations: storage memory mein hai, consent, sessions, key rotation aur rate limiting abhi nahi hain.
pitch.deep_5min:
Main request ke lifecycle se shuru karta hoon, src/server.ts ke order mein.

/authorize (handleAuthorize): pehle client_id aur redirect_uri. redirectUriAllowed sirf client.redirect_uris.includes() karta hai -- exact string. Tests mein 8 galat variants hain: prefix, trailing slash, extra query, doosra port, case, doosra host, doosre client ka URI, aur missing. In sab par 400 page, koi Location header nahi, koi cookie nahi. RFC 6749 4.1.2.1 kehta hai ki unverified URI par redirect mat karo.

Phir baaki checks, jinke errors redirect hote hain state aur iss ke saath: repeated parameter, response_type=code, response_mode sirf query, PKCE (code_challenge zaroori, method sirf S256 -- missing method ka matlab RFC 7636 mein plain hai, isliye woh bhi reject), scope client ke allowed list mein. prompt=none par login_required kyunki sessions hi nahi hain.

Valid request par ek LoginTransaction banta hai (id, csrfToken, validated params) aur cookie auth_tx mein id jaata hai (HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/login). Important: params server side rakhe hain, form se dobara trust nahi kiye.

/login (handleLogin): cookie se transaction, expiry check, phir safeEqual se CSRF token. Phir checkPassword: user mile toh verifySecret (scrypt, timingSafeEqual), na mile toh verifyAgainstDummy. 5 galat passwords par transaction khatam. Sahi par transaction delete (single use), code bana ke sirf sha256(code) store, aur 302 redirect code, state, iss ke saath.

/token (handleToken): pehle form parsing (content-type, duplicate params, 16 KiB limit), phir authenticateClient: Basic header ho toh confidential client aur scrypt secret check; na ho toh public client ka client_id; client_secret_post refuse. Phir codeGrant: codes.consume(hash) atomic hai -- pehli baar ok, baad mein reused. Reused par us code ki family revoke. Phir expiry, client, redirect_uri aur pkceMatches. Code pehli presentation par hi burn hota hai, chahe verifier galat ho.

sendTokens ek TokenFamily ke andar tokens deta hai: access token ES256 JWT (typ at+jwt, aud = issuer/userinfo, jti), jti -> family record hota hai; refresh token random, sha256 store; id_token aud = client_id, nonce, auth_time, at_hash.

refreshGrant: token hash se lookup, client match, family revoked nahi, expiry, scope sirf narrow. Phir markUsed atomic; agar false (pehle hi use ho chuka) toh reuseDetected poori family revoke karta hai. Naya refresh token usi family mein.

/userinfo: verifyJwt alg ko token se nahi leta -- hamesha ES256, typ at+jwt, kid se key, raw 64-byte signature, iss, aud, exp. Phir jti ki family revoked toh 401. Isliye id_token ko access token ki tarah bhejne par bhi 401.

Hardest decisions: JWT access tokens ka revocation sirf hamare userinfo par chalta hai, third party APIs ke liye 5 minute tak valid rehte hain. Revoke endpoint doosre client ke token par 200 deta hai aur kuch nahi karta, taaki pata na chale token exist karta hai. In-memory store ka check-and-set ek synchronous step hai, database mein UPDATE WHERE used=false chahiye.

Verification: 125 tests, 8 interop. 15 mutations: exact redirect, plain PKCE, verifier skip, reuse revoke, single use, expiry, family revoke, rotation, CSRF, client secret, signature, audience, state, no-store, revoke ownership -- sab pakde gaye. Rotation wale mutation par pehle sirf reuse test red hua tha; rotation test ka naam bolta tha 'old one stops working' par check nahi karta tha. Ab karta hai.
pitch.architecture_walkthrough:
src/secrets.ts: randomToken, sha256, safeEqual (dono side hash karke timingSafeEqual), scrypt hashSecret/verifySecret/verifyAgainstDummy (params hash ke andar), PKCE s256 aur pkceMatches.

src/jwt.ts: ES256 signJwt/verifyJwt node:crypto se (dsaEncoding ieee-p1363), JWK export, jwkThumbprint (RFC 7638 kid), atHash.

src/config.ts: validateConfig/loadConfig -- clients (public/confidential, exact redirect_uris, allowed_scopes, grant_types) aur users; plain text secrets ya http non-loopback redirect reject.

src/store.ts: TransactionStore, CodeStore, TokenStore interfaces aur Memory implementations. consume aur markUsed atomic hone chahiye.

src/http.ts: form parsing (duplicates reject, body limit), cookies, oauthError, no-store, HTML escaping aur security headers.

src/pages.ts: login form aur error page.

src/server.ts: createAuthHandler/createAuthServer aur saare endpoints: handleAuthorize, handleLogin, handleToken (codeGrant, refreshGrant), handleUserinfo, handleRevoke, discoveryDocument.

src/index.ts: CLI (CONFIG_FILE, PORT, HOST, ISSUER, SIGNING_KEY_FILE). src/hash-secret.ts: config ke liye scrypt hash.

test/: helpers.ts (ephemeral port server, injectable clock, login helpers), flow, authorize, login, token, refresh, userinfo, revoke, discovery, units, interop.
difficult_decisions: PKCE sabke liye zaroori, confidential clients ke liye bhi, aur sirf S256: missing method ko plain maan ke reject kiya.
Code pehli presentation par burn: galat verifier wala attempt bhi code khatam karta hai; client auth fail hone par nahi.
Token family: code reuse, refresh reuse aur revocation teeno poori family revoke karte hain, access tokens samet (userinfo par).
JWT access tokens: offline verify ho sakte hain, lekin third-party API ke liye revocation exp (300 s) tak nahi dikhta.
Revoke endpoint doosre client ke token par 200 aur kuch nahi karta (RFC 'refused' kehta hai; maine existence chhupana chuna).
Storage interfaces ke peeche in-memory: abhi simple, aur database ke liye atomic operations comments mein likhe.
biggest_challenges: ES256 signature format: node DER deta hai, JWS ko raw 64-byte r||s chahiye; dsaEncoding ieee-p1363 se sahi hua aur jose ne verify kiya.
openid-client ke saath interop: http test server ke liye allowInsecureRequests, aur id_token alg ES256 explicitly batana pada.
openid-client ka nonce error message generic tha; test ko wrapped error ke cause par check karna pada taaki pakka ho ki nonce hi reject hua.
Mutation check se ek kamzor test mila: rotation test ne purane token ko dobara try hi nahi kiya tha; fix karke red-green dobara dikhaya.
Refresh scope narrowing: rejected scope request token ko burn na kare, isliye scope check atomic markUsed se pehle rakha.
failure_scenarios: Server restart: DATA_DIR ke saath codes, refresh tokens, revocations, sessions aur keys bach jaate hain (sirf login forms jo khule the dobara shuru karne padte hain); bina DATA_DIR ke sab memory mein tha aur sab invalid.
Authorization code redirect se leak: PKCE verifier ke bina bekaar; agar legit client pehle redeem kar chuka toh attacker ka attempt family revoke kar deta hai.
Refresh token chori: attacker ya client mein se jo pehle use kare, doosre ka use reuse dikhata hai aur family revoke hoti hai.
Do processes chalaye toh: har process ka alag memory store, code ek process mein bana doosre mein unknown -- stage 1 single process hai.
Brute force login: per-transaction 5 attempts ke baad khatam, lekin naya transaction khol sakte hain; asli rate limiting nahi hai.
Access token chori: 300 s tak kisi bhi offline-verifying API par chalega; sender-constrained tokens (DPoP) nahi hain.
improvements: PostgreSQL store same interfaces ke peeche, atomic UPDATE ... WHERE used = false ke saath, aur do processes wala concurrency test.
Data dir lock, ek fsync per request, log lines par checksum, runtime compaction.
Keys KMS/HSM mein, compromised key ka emergency removal.
SSO: session cookie se prompt=none, max_age; logout confirmation page; back-channel logout.
Consent screen, login rate limiting, DPoP ya mTLS-bound tokens, introspection.
scrypt cost, fsync latency aur token endpoint throughput ka asli measurement.

steps: 1. Concept: code front channel se aata hai, tokens back channel se; PKCE code ko us client se bandhta hai jisne flow shuru kiya.
2. Project need: public clients (SPA) ke paas secret nahi hota, isliye PKCE hi code chori se bachata hai.
3. Code/API: server.ts handleAuthorize, codeGrant; secrets.ts s256, pkceMatches.
4. Detail: S256 only, missing method = plain = reject; verifier syntax RFC 7636 ke hisaab se check.
5. Demo: npx vitest run test/authorize.test.ts test/token.test.ts
6. Interviewer next: confidential client ko PKCE kyun? plain kab theek tha?
1. Concept: redirect_uri woh jagah hai jahan code jaata hai; galat URI = code attacker ke paas.
2. Project need: open redirect aur code theft se bachna.
3. Code/API: server.ts redirectUriAllowed, config.ts validateConfig.
4. Detail: exact string match; galat URI par redirect nahi, 400 page; http sirf loopback; fragment mana.
5. Demo: npx vitest run test/authorize.test.ts -t redirect_uri
6. Interviewer next: native apps ke loopback ports? Wildcard kyun khatarnak?

learning_path.concept: Refresh token rotation and reuse detection
steps: 1. Concept: har refresh par naya token; purana dobara aaye toh chori ka signal.
2. Project need: lambe chalne wale refresh tokens ki chori ka nuksan kam karna.
3. Code/API: server.ts refreshGrant, reuseDetected; store.ts TokenStore markUsed, revokeFamily.
4. Detail: token sirf hash ke roop mein store; family ek code se nikli saari cheezein.
5. Demo: npx vitest run test/refresh.test.ts
6. Interviewer next: legit client ka network retry bhi reuse lagega, toh? Grace period?

learning_path.concept: JWTs with ES256, JWKS and verification
steps: 1. Concept: JWS = header.payload.signature; JWKS public keys publish karta hai, kid se key chuni jaati hai.
2. Project need: resource servers bina humse baat kiye token verify kar sakein.
3. Code/API: jwt.ts signJwt, verifyJwt, jwkThumbprint, atHash.
4. Detail: ieee-p1363 signature, alg token se nahi liya jaata, typ at+jwt alag id_token se.
5. Demo: npx vitest run test/userinfo.test.ts test/interop.test.ts
6. Interviewer next: key rotation kaise? alg confusion attack kya hai?

learning_path.concept: Login form security: scrypt, CSRF, constant-time compare
steps: 1. Concept: slow password hash, synchronizer CSRF token, timing-safe comparisons.
2. Project need: password leak, login CSRF aur user enumeration se bachna.
3. Code/API: secrets.ts hashSecret, verifySecret, verifyAgainstDummy, safeEqual; server.ts handleLogin.
4. Detail: scrypt params hash mein; dummy scrypt unknown user par; CSRF token transaction cookie se bandha.
5. Demo: npx vitest run test/login.test.ts
6. Interviewer next: argon2 vs scrypt vs bcrypt? Rate limiting kahan?

learning_path.concept: Proving tests can fail: interop and mutation checks
steps: 1. Concept: green tests tabhi kuch saabit karte hain jab rule tootne par woh red hon.
2. Project need: security code mein 'test pass' ka matlab 'rule laga hai' hona chahiye.
3. Code/API: test/interop.test.ts (jose, openid-client), README ki mutation table.
4. Detail: 15 mutations, ek gap mila (rotation test) aur fix hua.
5. Demo: koi check tod ke (jaise redirectUriAllowed mein startsWith) npm test chalao, phir git checkout.
6. Interviewer next: mutation testing tools (Stryker)? Interop kyun zaroori?

learning_path.concept: Persistence, crash safety and key rotation (stage 2)
steps: 1. Concept: write-ahead append-only log + replay + compaction; keys ki next/active/retired lifecycle.
2. Project need: restart ke baad bhi single-use codes, reuse detection, revocations aur tokens ki verification sahi rahe.
3. Code/API: src/file-store.ts openFileStores, readLog, snapshot; src/keys.ts FileKeyRing; src/server.ts keyRetentionMs.
4. Detail: fsync pehle, apply baad mein; torn last line drop, beech ki kharab line par start fail; retired key = longest JWT lifetime tak published.
5. Demo: npx vitest run test/persistence.test.ts test/keys.test.ts test/interop.test.ts
6. Interviewer next: do processes same file par? Power loss? Key compromise?
1. Concept: RP browser ko OP ke end_session_endpoint par bhejta hai; OP session aur tokens khatam karta hai.
2. Project need: logout ke baad refresh tokens zinda na rahein; open redirect na bane.
